title: Multiplying Mixed Numbers
short: Rename as fractions, or use partial products.
trouble: Children multiply the whole parts and the fraction parts separately, so 2 1/2 × 2 1/2 comes out as 4 1/4.

blocks.html: You can multiply fractions and rename mixed numbers as fractions. Multiplying mixed numbers uses both skills.
Rename each mixed number as a fraction greater than 1, multiply the numerators and the denominators, then simplify and write the answer as a mixed number.

$2\frac{1}{2} \times 2\frac{1}{2}$ is the area of a square with sides $2\frac{1}{2}$. Splitting each side into $2 + \frac{1}{2}$ gives four parts: $2 \times 2 = 4$, two strips of $2 \times \frac{1}{2} = 1$, and a corner of $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{4}$. Total $6\frac{1}{4}$. Renaming as $\frac{5}{2} \times \frac{5}{2} = \frac{25}{4}$ gives the same, with less work.

blocks.cap: $2\frac{1}{2} \times 2\frac{1}{2}$ as an area. The two strips in the middle are what the common mistake leaves out.

blocks.title: A whole number times a mixed number

blocks.html: Multiplying the whole numbers and the fractions separately: $2\frac{1}{2} \times 2\frac{1}{2} = 4\frac{1}{4}$. The area model shows the two middle strips worth 1 each are missing. Check with an estimate: $2\frac{1}{2} \times 2\frac{1}{2}$ is more than $2 \times 3 = 6$.
